messages:
Sophie: Hey @support, ACME reported their app started getting 429s and their org token balance showed 0 at 23:55 local (Europe/Berlin). Their billing cycle says midnight UTC. They insist no plan change — why would tokens drop before midnight?
Alex: can you paste org id and tenant tz? Are they on promo or reserved capacity?
Sophie: org=acme-inc, tenant tz=Europe/Berlin, plan=pay-as-you-go, no promo or reserved.
SupportBot: Observability alert: quota-depletion event detected for org=acme-inc at 2025-11-30T23:55:12+01:00 (tokens_remaining=0).
Ben: 23:55 CET is 22:55 UTC — odd since refill is 00:00 UTC. Possible culprits: sustained streaming sessions + rapid reconnects, or multiple subprojects hitting shared org bucket. Ask for request ids and sample logs.
Maria: Sophie, please grab X-Request-Id headers from one of the 429 responses and a short sample of timestamped requests. Also confirm whether they were using websocket streaming or standard REST.
Sophie: pasted customer logs snippet:
```
2025-11-30T23:54:58+01:00 GET /v1/generate 200 X-Req: req_aa
2025-11-30T23:55:11+01:00 POST /v1/stream 429 X-Req: req_bb
2025-11-30T23:55:30+01:00 POST /v1/generate 429 X-Req: req_cc
```
They say a websocket stream had been open for multiple hours prior.
Ben: that matches a common pattern: long-lived streams with intermittent reconnects can trigger bursts of token accounting, especially if each reconnect results in a full usage delta. Also if their client retried aggressively on 429, it can amplify drain.
Alex: I'll check platform logs for refill job timing. There was a delayed maintenance earlier this month that caused a refill lag once, but that was different. Also verify subproject aggregation — sometimes devteams unknowingly share the org bucket.
Maria: quick ops check: org shows a usage ramp from 23:30–23:56 CET with concentrated spikes at 23:54–23:56. No promo flags detected, no reserved capacity. Looks like streaming reconnect storm + per-connection accounting exhausted the bucket before UTC midnight.
Sophie: Customer also says UI showed 'refilled' at 00:00 UTC but their API still returned 429 for ~30s after. How do we explain the visible discrepancy?
Ben: UI reads edge-cached billing snapshots (TTL ~15s). Refill job marks the billing ledger at 00:00 UTC then replication to edge caches and token counters can take a short propagation window. API checks authoritative counters and may require replication to finish, so you can see UI update slightly sooner or later than API depending on region. If delay >5min we escalate.
Maria: Action items: 1) Sophie -> share full logs and X-Request-Id list to ops. 2) Ops -> verify refill cron ran at 00:00 UTC and check token-counter replication lag. 3) Recommend customer: reduce streaming keepalive frequency, add session timeouts, avoid aggressive client retries. 4) Offer 1-hour courtesy top-up while we investigate. :thumbsup:
Sophie: shared request ids with ops and informed customer. They accepted the courtesy top-up. Assigning to @ops to confirm refill job and replication metrics; will close thread after ops confirms everything reconciled.
